Subject: Renewal planning and capacity needs (Q1-Q3 2027)

Hi Evelyn,

We're kicking off renewal discussions for our Dedicated deployment (contract ends 2026-12-31). We've seen a pretty sharp increase in model traffic since July after the product relaunch: current 95th percentile QPS ~1,200 and average request size ~145 tokens (seq=145). Peak token throughput is ~174k tokens/s across the fleet. We expect continued growth as two new features roll out in Q1 2027; conservative forecast is ~2.5x by end of Q2 2027, aggressive is ~3.5x.

Can Redwood propose a recommended reserved GPU sizing and an approach to avoid a hard capacity cutover at renewal? Procurement also asked for an attachment showing quarterly usage. Attaching the exported usage CSV from our telemetry.

Thanks — Sarah

Hi Sarah — appreciate the data. We'll put together a phased expansion proposal that smooths capacity increases across the renewal term and avoids a single large provisioning event.

What we'll include in the proposal:
- Normalized throughput assumptions (we'll normalize to tokens/sec and request QPS at 128/256/512 avg seq lengths).
- Baseline reserved pool to cover sustained 95th percentile with a small burst buffer.
- Phased add-ons (timed to your product milestones) implemented as reserved increments + burst pools for peak events.
- Suggested SLA/throughput guardrails and a short-term bridging discount for the first 3 months of the renewed term.

Can you confirm whether the new features will increase average sequence length (expected) and whether KV-cache hit rates are likely to improve (we saw a 12% hit rate in Q3). Also looping Karthik and Monica to help size GPUs and costs.

Best,

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:03:08 -0800
Subject: Argentum renewal — initial sizing math (internal)

Team — quick working notes before we draft the customer-facing proposal. I normalized Argentum's CSV to tokens/sec assuming mean seq=160 (they said seq will increase). Key current metrics (Q3/Q4 aggregated):
- Current sustained 95th QPS: 1,200 req/s
- Avg tokens per request (current): 145; projected steady-state: 160; peak feature window: 220
- Current peak tokens/sec: ~174,000 tps
- Observed KV cache hit: 12% (inefficient today)

Throughput baseline per GPU (observed on Redwood Dedicated A100p-80GB, quantized model profile):
- At 160 seq avg: ~28k tokens/s per GPU sustained with small-burst headroom
- At 220 seq avg: ~20k tokens/s per GPU

Sizing options (rounded):
- Conservative (1.5x growth by Q2): add +8 GPUs (reserved) now => total reserved + burst to cover ~420k tps projected peak
- Recommended phased (min disruption): add +8 GPUs on renewal start (Month 0), add another +16 GPUs in Q2 (Month 4) as feature rollouts land => effective capacity ~720k tps by Q2
- Aggressive (3x growth): immediate +24 GPUs reserved to avoid any burst risk.

Other recommendations:
- Include a 20% burst pool (preemptible/burstable capacity) to handle short windows while saving commit costs.
- Commit term: extend to 18 months with a front-loaded 3-month bridging discount (10%) to help Argentum transition traffic and to align billing with product ramp.
- Add an auto-fallback policy to route low-latency traffic to a lower-cost model variant if sustained latency increases >150 ms P50.

I'll convert this into a clear table and pricing delta for the customer doc. Monica — can you run a cost delta for Reserved+Burst vs Immediate Full Reserve and add an ops note about delivery lead time for +24 GPUs?

- Evelyn

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@argentum.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Argentum Procurement <procurement@argentum.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:45 -0800
Subject: Proposal — Phased Renewal & Bridging Plan (Argentum Dedicated)

Sarah / team — attached is a proposal (redwood_phased_proposal_v2.pdf) and an SLA addendum draft. High level summary below; full line-item pricing in the PDF.

Proposal summary (key bullets):
- Term: 18 months (renewal start 2027-01-01) with a 3-month bridging discount at 10% on computation for Months 0-3.
- Phased reserved GPU additions: +8 GPUs (reserved) Month 0; +16 GPUs (reserved) Month 4. Total added reserved: 24 GPUs over 4 months.
- Burst pool: 20% of committed capacity allocated as burstable instances (fast provisioning, separate pool) for peak windows.
- Throughput SLOs: sustained 95th token throughput guarantee tied to committed GPUs. Operational SLO: 99.5% availability for committed capacity; 95% availability for burst pool.
- Performance assumptions used: mean seq 160 (month 0), rising to 200 by Month 4; tokens/sec per GPU estimated accordingly (28k -> 22k tps).
- Fallback policy: automatic model variant fallback and regional routing if sustained P50 latency moves above 150 ms.

Why phased: avoids a single large invoice and reduces cold-start risk. It also lets us tune KV-cache and batching after the initial +8 GPUs to improve tokens/sec/GPU before committing the larger uplift. We estimate this reduces total committed GPUs by ~6 compared to immediate full reserve because efficiency improves.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm you accept phased approach (reply to this thread).
2) Procurement to review PDF & SLA addendum and confirm redlines.
3) We prepare a DocuSign package (I attached the draft SLA addendum) and schedule a rollout kick-off with Ops for 48-hour provisioning windows for each add-on.

Attachments: redwood_phased_proposal_v2.pdf; SLA_addendum_draft.docx

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
